posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Setting the permissions for the subfolder would mean that the unprivileged user can still see the backup folder even though he has --- permission for it. This is because the ability to view the name of a directory depends on the permission of its parent directory, and not on its own permission. So to make it secure you would have to set the restrictive permission on the parent directory itself.

Hope this helps.

Screenshot 2024-10-30 at 1.21.18 AM940×870 51.2 KB

posts.name: Tushar Verma
posts.cooked:
@sayan,
That’s true and I understand that ability to view depends on the parent directory because that specific file/ directory is content of the parent directory.

However, my question was more about the language and instructions given in the question. It wasn’t clear that permissions need to be blocked for directory and/or backup files, i.e. what the question is exactly asking.

Now backup files are a part of data directory and that’s why to prevent viewing the backup files permissions of data directory needs to be modified but -

  1. The ask/ need to block “viewing” of the backup files was not indicated in the question.
  2. It is hard to assume and move forward. Consider this sceanrio, you typically won’t block access if you are working in a team/ group/ shared system with multiple users. For ex: 2 DBAs are working on a project and share the data directory to access and store the backups. In that case you would keep permissions on for the group as well. Limiting write access to directory will prohibit the other user(s) to make backups in that directory. Here we would only like to change the permissions of files and not the directory.

All this lead to ambiguity in the question during the quiz and that’s what I am trying to highlight. I urge the course team to look into this and consider.

Regards,
Tushar Verma
